title: Binary consequences of relation-liveness automata lower bounds
description: Explicit fixed-binary-alphabet consequences of OpenAI's two relation-liveness lower bounds. A strict h-squared adjacency-block language has a one-way nondeterministic source with (3h^3-h)/2+2 endmarked states, and an ordinary epsilon-free source with one fewer state. Equivalent two-way deterministic automata and two-way nondeterministic automata for its full binary complement require 2^Omega(h), hence 2^Omega(n^(1/3)) in the cubic source size. The note gives exact transitions, an sh^2-state pullback, all-word complement semantics, and an h^3 fooling-set source lower bound. The exponential obstructions are inherited from OpenAI; binary coding is established machinery, attributed to earlier work. AI tools were used extensively. This preprint has not undergone conventional human peer review or refereeing. Automated proof and package audits are documented. Upstream Lean build, axiom printing and Comparator validation were not reproduced due local disk exhaustion; neither reproduced formal verification nor binary formalization is claimed.

title: Hypersingular Riesz-energy constants on surfaces from triangular-lattice universal optimality
description:
This consequence note records the exact ordered-pair two-dimensional hypersingular Riesz-energy constant for every real s > 2: C_(s,2) = zeta_Lambda(s), with Lambda the covolume-one triangular lattice. For every smooth compact embedded surface with positive area A, including smooth boundary and using ambient Euclidean distance, the minimal ordered energy is asymptotic to zeta_Lambda(s) A^(-s/2) N^(1+s/2). The unit sphere coefficient is zeta_Lambda(s)/(4 pi)^(s/2).

OpenAI's recently released planar universal-energy theorem is the substantive new input. The finite/periodic reduction and manifold universality are established results of Hardin, Saff, Simanek, Leble and Serfaty, with periodic averaging credited to Cohn and Kumar. We give a self-contained gap-periodization account with exact pair, density, covolume and tail conventions. The target is the dimension-two s > 2 case of Brauchart-Hardin-Saff Conjecture 2, originally posed for the sphere by Kuijlaars and Saff. No independent base breakthrough or first-public-priority claim is made.

The upstream analytic arguments were independently audited and their finite certificates reproduced. Actual Lean source semantics were inspected, but a complete pinned Lean/Mathlib build was not reproduced; no formal-verification claim is made. AI tools were used extensively in research, drafting and verification. title: Even Minkowski uniqueness as a consequence of logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski
description: This research note records consequences of OpenAI's recently released origin-symmetric logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski inequality. In every ambient dimension n >= 2 and for 0 <= p < 1, every smooth strictly positive even density on S^(n-1) has exactly one smooth positive even support-function solution of h^(1-p) det(∇²h+hI)=f with positive-definite curvature-radius matrix. For 0 < p < 1, identical Lp surface-area measures determine arbitrary full-dimensional origin-symmetric convex bodies. The note gives the nonsmooth first-variation and mixed-volume strictness argument explicitly and a local form of the smooth endpoint transfer of He–Liu; existence and regularity are established inputs. These results are newly available consequences of the new inequality and known reductions, not a new proof of logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski or a claim of first public announcement. Equal-volume boxes exclude arbitrary-measure uniqueness at p=0. The package contains source, analytic and priority audits, pinned dependency hashes and reproducible exact rational checks. The upstream Lean source scope was inspected, but independent kernel rebuilding, axiom extraction and Comparator reproduction were not completed; no formal verification of this follow-on theorem is claimed. title: Pure-loss bosonic dynamic capacities: EPnI consequences and consumed-key secrecy accounting
description: The finite-energy multimode entropy photon-number inequality in the OpenAI mathematics release supplies the sharp entropy premise for the previously conditional pure-loss bosonic classical/quantum/entanglement capacity region under an average photon constraint, including arbitrary entanglement across channel uses. This note gives the precise consequence and audits a private-resource operational defect: the printed catalytic secrecy condition in the cited coding theorem protects consumed key jointly with generated secrets and excludes the one-time pad. A zero-energy converse refutes the displayed private region under that literal condition. The public/private/secret-key formula is proved under an explicitly corrected generated-secret trace-secrecy convention, with corrected converse accounting and direct key-assisted coding. The formulas and conditional reductions are inherited; this is not an independent proof of EPnI or a full solution of the false unchanged private target. The upstream unrefereed EPnI proof was analytically audited; its Lean build was not reproduced. AI tools were used extensively in research, drafting and verification. title: Two consequences of group-algebra and planar Fourier certificates: wreath products and triangle bounds
description: We derive two separately motivated consequences of precisely identified input theorems in OpenAI's mathematics collection. The torsion-free group-algebra counterexample, combined with the established Hopfian embedding framework, yields a finitely generated Hopfian group H for which the standard restricted regular wreath product C2 wr H is non-Hopfian. We give its split epimorphism and kernel explicitly. The sharp planar two-point Fourier certificate, combined with the Cohn-de Laat-Salmon product-program comparison and triangular-lattice Poisson bounds, yields L2=2/sqrt(3) and the exact planar triangle infimum P2=4/3. We reconstruct the deductions, audit the substantive inputs, repair product-proof bookkeeping, and provide independently implemented validated computations and source records. These consequences use credited literature; no first-priority or independent-breakthrough claim is made. The planar equality does not settle the all-dimensional triangle problem or assert attainment of its infimum. AI tools were used extensively in research, drafting, computation and verification. Internal independent and adversarial reviews were AI-assisted. This preprint has not undergone conventional human peer review or refereeing. AI systems are not authors; no external endorsement is implied. The associated Lean artifacts concern another construction and do not formally verify these results.

title: An explicit complex polynomial retract in five variables: a consequence of affine-space cancellation failure
description: Using OpenAI's explicit complex cancellation fourfold, this consequence note gives split complex-algebra maps and a five-component idempotent polynomial endomorphism of affine five-space whose image has transcendence degree four and is not a polynomial algebra. The cylinder-to-retract implication is classical, as recorded by Nagamine; the cancellation example, stabilization and nonpolynomiality are attributed to OpenAI. The four-variable retract question is not settled. The package includes exact symbolic certificates, written dependency audits and a bounded priority audit. title: Signed impulse estimates and global smooth solutions for finite multispecies relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell
description: This research note extends the signed-impulse argument of OpenAI family 362 to a fixed finite number of relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell species with positive masses and arbitrary real charges. It derives the exact source-receiver coefficient, positive mass-weighted energy, angular occupation and selected coefficient bounds, and one coupled momentum bootstrap. The stated global classical theorem assumes nonnegative smooth compact phase data and compatible Maxwell fields with bounded derivatives of all orders and finite energy. The one-species result and its analytic machinery are attributed to OpenAI; mass normalization and continuation are established kinetic theory. No firstness or full Lean-formalization claim is made. The universal geometric cancellation is inherited; the new contribution is its species-dependent coefficient transfer and coupled closure for distinct charge-to-mass ratios. title: A priori estimates across the subcritical Lane–Emden hyperbola
description:
This consequence note records the full strictly subcritical Lane–Emden estimate package for n at least 3 and p,q greater than 1: universal pointwise and gradient estimates on arbitrary proper domains, exterior decay, zero-Dirichlet half-space nonexistence without a growth assumption, and fixed bounded C2-domain Dirichlet bounds and strong compactness in exact spaces. It applies the OpenAI 2026 entire Liouville theorem to established Polacik–Quittner–Souplet and Quittner–Souplet reductions, with an explicit normalization and boundary blow-up account. title: L2-acyclicity and cost for a rank-100 amalgam
description:
An expanded consequence and verification note for OpenAI's rank-100 fixed-price construction. A self-contained regular-tree and cellular-boundary calculation proves that its displayed 101-generator/100-relator presentation complex is a finite two-dimensional classifying space and every L2-Betti number vanishes, independently of either cost bound. Gaboriau's action invariance and OpenAI's positive Bernoulli cost estimate then give an explicit free ergodic p.m.p. orbit relation with Cost at least 1 + 1/(100*2^61) and vanishing L2-Betti numbers. The group infimum cost is one.

The group and positive cost estimate are due to OpenAI; cost--Betti comparison and action invariance are due to Gaboriau. The general fixed-price implication was already explicit in Popa--Shlyakhtenko--Vaes, and the short conditional limit argument was already in the author's public preliminary triage. Added content is the direct all-degree invariant proof and reproducible input-validation record. No independent fixed-price discovery or firstness is claimed. The pinned upstream source warns that its source argument was intermediate. Its pivotal proof is explicitly identified and independently audited in the supplement.

title: Rational Hodge classes on mixed products of K3 moduli spaces
description: Combining OpenAI's rational Hodge theorem for arbitrary mixed products of projective K3 surfaces with Bülles' Chow-motive decomposition, this note records rational Hodge in every codimension for finite mixed products of the smooth projective K3 moduli spaces covered by that decomposition. Bases may differ or repeat. The factors include Hilbert schemes, stable twisted-sheaf moduli, and eligible moduli of Bridgeland-stable objects, subject to the exact smoothness, projectivity and stability hypotheses stated in the paper. The explicit pull-push proof checks codimensions and the non-fine, empty and zero-dimensional cases. The contribution is an assembled corollary of the cited results, with prior conditional transfers by Arapura; it supplies no new proof of the base K3 theorem, no new motivic reduction, and no first or substantial independent novelty claim. The base input is the public OpenAI Math Release snapshot adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a, accessed October 6, 2026: https://github.com/openai/math/tree/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a. title: Reduced C*-algebras of the Thompson family: an attributed consequence of nonamenability
description: An attributed consequence note applying OpenAI's nonamenability theorem for standard Thompson F to the published equivalences of Le Boudec and Matte Bon. The reduced group C*-algebras of F, T, the full automorphism group Aut(F), and the abstract commensurator Comm(F) are simple and have their canonical traces as their unique tracial states, by the discrete-group trace theorem of Breuillard, Kalantar, Kennedy and Ozawa. The countable standard circle-overgroup consequence is also recorded. All these simplicity reductions are inherited; T's unique trace was already unconditional. title: Exact semidefinite complexity of the symmetric traveling-salesman polytope
description: The exponential real PSD-rank theorem for shifted perfect-matching matrices in the OpenAI Math Release implies that the symmetric traveling-salesman polytope on N cities has exact real semidefinite extension complexity 2^Theta(N), measured by the order of one real PSD matrix (or total block order). This concise consequence note gives explicit data for Yannakakis's established 3n-city face projection, a 2n-city contraction variant, all-city-count padding, an exact affine-slack calculation, and the subset-state flow upper bound 2(N-1)+(N-1)(N-2)2^(N-3). The lower-bound breakthrough is attributed to OpenAI; no new lower-bound method or firstness claim is made. title: Bilinear ergodic Hilbert variation for commuting transformations as a consequence of annular triangular variation
description: We give an explicit restriction and transference consequence of OpenAI's full annular variation theorem for the triangular Hilbert transform, manuscript dated October 5, 2026, at source commit adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a. For arbitrary commuting invertible probability-preserving transformations S,T and complex f,g in L3, the symmetric sums H_N=sum_(0<|n|<=N) f(S^n x)g(T^n x)/n, with H_0=0, satisfy a pointwise r-variation estimate in L^(3/2) for every r>2. They have a bounded maximum and converge almost everywhere and in L^(3/2), with maximal-tail convergence in that norm. The proof uses fixed positive-area cell boxes, half-integer radial endpoints, an explicitly summable O(k^-2) signed kernel error, and finite-menu finite-window Calderon transference. The continuous analytic breakthrough is inherited and credited; this note supplies its discrete restriction and ergodic consequence. Classical transference and its modern predecessors are credited, and no first-priority or independent triangular-Hilbert breakthrough claim is made. Scope remains L3 inputs, symmetric odd truncations, commuting transformations and r>2; there is no r=2, noncommuting or one-sided Cesaro claim. title: The Sperner property of standard graded Artinian complete intersections in characteristic zero
description: For every standard graded Artinian complete intersection over an arbitrary characteristic-zero field, the maximum minimal number of generators over all ideals, including nonhomogeneous ideals, equals the largest coefficient of the complete-intersection Hilbert series. This concise note records an immediate consequence of OpenAI's Artinian EGH theorem and the previously published EGH-to-Sperner implication of Harima, Wachi and Watanabe. It makes degree-one elimination, the empty/all-linear case, the all-ideal filtration argument and field scope explicit, with exact integer examples and scoped dependency/priority audits. title: Metric rigidity at the boundary of cubic compactifications
description: This note deduces a sharp Cartier-index criterion for irreducible normal projective complex klt Fano varieties of positive dimension carrying a weak Kahler–Einstein metric with bounded potentials: an ample Cartier root -K_X = rL with r > dim(X)/2 + 1 forces stable tangent sheaves on finite quasi-etale covers and rigidity of parallel orthogonal complex structures up to sign. The criterion combines the decomposition theorem of Druel–Guenancia–Paun, a Hilbert-polynomial index bound, and local positive-Ricci curvature; products of equal-dimensional projective spaces show that the strict threshold is sharp. For cubic n-folds with n at least 5, the note applies the criterion to identify all fibers of the forgetful map from complex-preserving GH moduli to ordinary metric GH moduli as conjugation orbits, including singular boundary points. This cubic application uses as an external input OpenAI's ordinary-double-point upper gap theorem at repository commit adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a; that theorem is not reproved here. The complex-preserving cubic GH/GIT comparison is an attributed deduction through Li–Liu's global Reeb minimum and Spotti–Sun's established transfer. Kong–Shen–Zhao–Zhao already publicly state a stronger complex algebraic comparison. Smooth tangent stability, smooth metric rigidity, and the conjugation convention are credited to Peternell–Wisniewski, Spotti, and Odaka–Spotti–Sun. No first-solution claim, scheme or stack comparison, or formal verification is made. The downloadable files are the paper PDF and an archive of original source, verification scripts, scoped audits, and provenance records; third-party manuscripts and reading caches are excluded. title: Output-sensitive sparse factorization over finite fields from dense factorization
description: We give a deterministic reduction for complete sparse univariate polynomial factorization over explicitly represented finite fields. The bit cost is polynomial in term count, binary exponent length, field encoding and the total degree of the distinct densely returned factors, with arbitrary binary multiplicities. A sparse numerator and dense denominator are maintained through characteristic-p descent; denominator degree grows by at most the original radical degree per step. Classical Pade reconstruction, logarithmic derivatives, residue multiplicity methods and Cartier sections are attributed to their original sources. The paper also details inherited dense factorization and prescribed-degree irreducible construction consequences of OpenAI family142 through Berlekamp, Shoup and Rai. The upstream prime-field theorem requires family029 general cyclotomic Hecke zero-freeness. No randomness, GRH or integer-factorization oracle is introduced. Construction degree and optional fixed-root degree are numeric dense parameters; no general binary-degree construction/root bound or practical efficiency is claimed. The sparse theorem is not a sparse-output GCD or arbitrary-circuit theorem. Alec Kriebel is the sole author. AI tools were used extensively in research, drafting and verification. title: A sharp dyadic threshold in a characteristic-two random-cone construction
description: OpenAI's October 4 torsion-free group-algebra construction fixes a projective-plane order of 128. This note proves that 32 is the least dyadic order at least 4 at which the unchanged seven-extra squared turn weights admit exponential word-mass decay, using an exact three-class quotient and rational upper and lower certificates. Checking every affected estimate carries the source construction to a 532-edge rose. This is a model-specific threshold, not global generator optimality. Classical HNN embedding gives a two-generator realization; the scalar idempotent and absorbed nonzero cyclic projective right module are inherited consequences already recorded in public triage, and remain valid over every characteristic-two field. The matching is existential; no numerical group-ring multiplication certificate or full formalization is claimed. AI tools were used extensively in research, drafting and verification. title: Rational-point undecidability for smooth projective varieties over the rational numbers
description: Combining OpenAI's negative solution of rational Hilbert's tenth problem, with two explicit proof corrections documented in the verification package, and Poonen's established effective transfer, this note proves undecidability of rational-point existence for arbitrary smooth projective geometrically integral varieties over Q. It specifies homogeneous-equation presentations and valid-input oracle use, and rules out a computable uniform bound on the height of one point in terms of presentation size. Dimension and all size parameters may vary. The arithmetic breakthrough is attributed to OpenAI and the geometric reduction to Poonen; no independent solution of rational Hilbert's tenth problem, new geometric reduction, fixed-dimensional theorem, many-one hardness or first-priority claim is made. title: Nonnegative binary rational hafnians: an exact reduction and approximation and sampling consequences
description:
This note records a self-contained exact reduction from every even-order symmetric matrix with binary nonnegative rational off-diagonal entries to a simple unweighted perfect-matching count, with polynomial encoding length, an explicit logarithmic integer-weight gadget, exact rational scaling, and weighted matching fibers. Citing the general-graph FPRAS of OpenAI, it derives a uniform rational hafnian FPRAS with exact zero detection and a rigorously specified bounded-bit total-variation approximate sampler.
